svg.title: Identity, local authority and secret boundaries
svg.desc: External verified identities map to local scoped grants. Native services enforce authority before scoped transactions and credential resolution. Migration, app, scheduler and worker identities are distinct.
svg.text: Identity, local authority and secret boundaries
Identity proves who called. Local grants decide what the caller may do.
External identity / trusted host
Configured issuer, audience, client and token type
Signature verification or verified-identity port
Keycloak initial profile; other CIAM needs proof
Local principal + scoped grants
Explicit provider / issuer / subject link
Tenant / project / environment / resource limits
Role checks also run inside native services
Scoped transaction
Service actor + audit context + UoW
Transaction-local tenant context
PostgreSQL RLS and composite scoped keys
Credential and egress admission
Scoped secret handle, never workflow literal
Standing source or live worker lease authority
Explicit external origin / network policy
Separate operational identities
Migration owner applies DDL; app sessions are nonowner and cannot bypass RLS.
Scheduler enumeration is separate. Remote workers do not receive either database URL.
Provider role claims, URL scope, compiler success and secret names do not grant authority.
